title.zh: 卷343 列傳一百三十 书麟弟：广厚 觉罗吉庆 觉罗长麟 费淳 百龄 伯麟
title.en: Volume 343 Biographies 130: Shu Lin younger brother: Guang Hou, Jue Luo Ji Qing, Jue Luo Zhang Lin, Fei Chun, Bai Ling, Bo Lin
title.raw: 卷343 列傳一百三十 书麟弟：广厚 觉罗吉庆 觉罗长麟 费淳 百龄 伯麟

sentences.zh: 書麟，字紱齋，高佳氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人，大學士高晉子。

translations.literal: Shu Lin, courtesy name Fuzhai, of the Gaojia clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner, son of Grand Secretary Gao Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Lin, whose courtesy name was Fuzhai, belonged to the Gaojia clan and the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner; he was the son of Grand Secretary Gao Jin.

sentences.zh: 初授鑾儀衛整儀尉，累遷冠軍使，擢西安副都統。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed Ceremonial Guard orderly officer, was repeatedly promoted to Champion Messenger, and was raised to Vice Commander at Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: He began as an orderly officer in the Ceremonial Guard, rose through successive posts to Champion Messenger, and was then promoted to vice commander at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十八年，大軍徵金川，命為領隊大臣，從參贊大臣豐升額，力戰輒先登，克堅碉數十，功最。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Qianlong, when the great army campaigned against Jinchuan, he was ordered to serve as expedition leader, following Commissioner Feng Sheng'e; in fierce fighting he was always first to scale the walls, captured dozens of strong stockades, and had the greatest merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 38, when the imperial forces marched against Jinchuan, he was named expedition leader under Commissioner Feng Sheng'e; in hard fighting he repeatedly led the assault, took dozens of fortified stockades, and won the highest distinction.

sentences.zh: 金川平，加等議敘，圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: When Jinchuan was pacified, he received graded commendation for merit and had his portrait placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinchuan was pacified, his service was rewarded with graded honors, and his likeness was enshrined in the Hall of Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 授廣西巡撫，以父憂去。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Guangxi and left office on account of mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Guangxi but resigned when his father died.

sentences.zh: 起，署兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was recalled and served as acting Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning, he served as acting vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，出為安徽巡撫，歲旱，請留漕糧五萬石、關稅銀三十五萬兩賑之。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he went out as Governor of Anhui; the year was drought-stricken, and he requested that fifty thousand piculs of grain transport tribute and three hundred fifty thousand taels of customs silver be retained for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year he became governor of Anhui; when drought struck that year, he asked to retain fifty thousand piculs of transport grain and 350,000 taels of customs revenue for famine relief.

sentences.zh: 阜陽有荒地六千餘頃，疏請寬限清釐，民間交易用官弓丈量，以杜欺隱，期於漸復舊額。

translations.literal: In Fuyang there were more than six thousand qing of wasteland; he memorialized requesting an extended deadline for clearance and survey, that private transactions use the official measuring bow for surveying to stop concealment and fraud, with the aim of gradually restoring the old quota.
translations.idiomatic: More than six thousand qing of wasteland lay in Fuyang; he petitioned for more time to clear and register it, required private land deals to be measured with the official survey bow to curb fraud, and aimed to restore the former tax quota over time.

sentences.zh: 帝以書麟盡心民瘼，予優敘。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Shu Lin devoted himself to the people's hardships, granted him superior commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded him with special commendation for his devoted attention to the people's distress.

sentences.zh: 黃、運兩河漫溢，帝因兩江總督李世傑未諳河工，命書麟佐之。

translations.literal: The Yellow and Transport Rivers overflowed; because the Governor-General of the Two Jiangs, Li Shijie, was not versed in river works, the Emperor ordered Shu Lin to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow and Grand Canal rivers burst their banks, the emperor had Shu Lin assist Governor-General Li Shijie of the Two Jiangs, who was unfamiliar with hydraulic engineering.

sentences.zh: 與世傑及河督李奉翰議，漫口有四，惟司家莊、湯家莊兩處分溜，急興工堵築；

translations.literal: Together with Shijie and River Commissioner Li Fenghan they deliberated: there were four overflow points, but only at Sijiazhuang and Tangjiazhuang did the current divide; they urgently undertook works to block and build dikes.
translations.idiomatic: He conferred with Li Shijie and River Commissioner Li Fenghan: of four breach points, only Sijiazhuang and Tangjiazhuang were diverting flow, and they urgently launched dike-building works there.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「桃源境內河流因順黃壩生有淤灘，水勢紆折不暢。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Within Taoyuan the river, because of the Shunhuang Dam, had formed silt bars, and the current wound about without flowing freely.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported: "In Taoyuan the river had silted up below the Shunhuang Dam, so the current meandered sluggishly.

sentences.zh: 於玉皇閣下挑引河，俾黃流東注會清，以資宣洩。

translations.literal: Below the Jade Emperor Pavilion a diversion channel should be cut so that the Yellow current may flow east to join the Qing River and thereby provide discharge.
translations.idiomatic: A cut should be made below the Jade Emperor Pavilion to send the Yellow River east into the Qing River and ease the flood.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，擢兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he was promoted to Governor-General of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year he was raised to governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 書麟素行清謹，出巡屬邑，輕騎減從，民不擾累，特詔嘉之。

translations.literal: Shu Lin had always conducted himself with integrity and caution; when touring subordinate districts he used light mounts and reduced escort, the people were not troubled or burdened, and he received a special edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Lin was known for probity and restraint; on inspection tours he traveled lightly with a small escort so the people were not burdened, and the throne issued a special commendation.

sentences.zh: 和珅柄政，書麟與之忤。

translations.literal: When Heshen held power, Shu Lin was at odds with him.
translations.idiomatic: After Heshen came to dominate the government, Shu Lin fell out with him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有高郵巡檢陳倚道揭報書吏假印重徵事，遣重臣鞫實，坐書麟瞻徇，下部嚴議；

translations.literal: Before long, Gaoyou Inspector Chen Yidao exposed a case of clerks using forged seals to levy extra taxes; a high minister was sent to investigate, and Shu Lin was found guilty of shielding wrongdoers and referred to the ministries for severe deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward a Gaoyou inspector named Chen Yidao exposed clerks who had used forged seals to collect excess taxes; the court sent a senior official to investigate, found Shu Lin guilty of favoritism, and referred the case for severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 又失察句容書吏侵用錢糧，褫職，遣戍伊犁。

translations.literal: He was also found negligent in the case of Jurong clerks embezzling tax funds, was stripped of office, and banished to garrison duty at Yili.
translations.idiomatic: He was further faulted for failing to detect Jurong clerks who had misappropriated tax grain, stripped of rank, and exiled to Yili.

sentences.zh: 尋起為山西巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled and appointed Governor of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and made governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 內閣學士尹壯圖論州縣虧空由於派累，疆臣中惟李世傑、書麟獨善其身，和珅尤忌之，命壯圖赴各省清查倉庫，自山西始，壯圖因獲譴。

translations.literal: Grand Secretariat Academician Yin Zhuangtu argued that prefectural and county deficits arose from cumulative exactions; among frontier officials only Li Shijie and Shu Lin kept themselves clean, and Heshen especially resented them; he ordered Zhuangtu to go to each province to audit granaries, beginning in Shanxi, and Zhuangtu was punished as a result.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Yin Zhuangtu of the Grand Secretariat argued that local deficits came from cumulative exactions; of the frontier governors only Li Shijie and Shu Lin had kept their hands clean, which Heshen especially resented. Heshen sent Zhuangtu to audit provincial granaries, starting in Shanxi, and Zhuangtu was punished in the affair.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，仍授兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he was again appointed Governor-General of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year he was again made governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 兩淮鹽政巴寧阿交結商人，坐書麟徇庇，复奪職，予三等侍衛，赴新疆效力。

translations.literal: Lianghuai Salt Controller Baning'a had colluded with merchants; Shu Lin was found guilty of shielding him, was again stripped of office, was given the rank of third-class bodyguard, and sent to Xinjiang to redeem himself by service.
translations.idiomatic: When Lianghuai salt controller Baning'a was found in league with merchants, Shu Lin was again dismissed for covering for him, given the rank of third-class bodyguard, and sent to Xinjiang on penal service.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，和珅敗，召授吏部尚書，兼正紅旗漢軍都統，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, when Heshen fell, he was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel, concurrently Commander of the Plain Red Banner Chinese Martial Forces, with the added title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4, after Heshen's downfall, he was recalled as minister of personnel, made commander of the Plain Red Chinese Martial Banner, and given the title junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋協辦大學士，授閩浙總督。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Associate Grand Secretary and appointed Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made associate grand secretary and governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 弟廣興，以首發和珅姦擢官，既得官，多所彈擊，書麟不善所為，嘗於帝前言之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Guangxing, because he was first to expose Heshen's crimes, was promoted; once in office he impeached many people, and Shu Lin disapproved of his conduct and once spoke of it before the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Guangxing had won promotion for being first to denounce Heshen; once in office Guangxing impeached many officials, and Shu Lin disapproved—he once told the emperor so.

sentences.zh: 至是，廣興以掌四川軍需獲咎，書麟請嚴治，且自引罪，詔宥之。

translations.literal: At this time Guangxing was punished for managing Sichuan military supplies; Shu Lin asked that he be severely dealt with and himself accepted blame, but an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangxing was punished for mismanaging Sichuan military supplies, Shu Lin asked for strict punishment and took blame upon himself, but the throne pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 調雲貴，鞫前督富綱，得其貪婪狀，論如律；

translations.literal: He was transferred to Yunnan-Guizhou, tried the former governor Fu Gang, obtained proof of his greed, and sentenced him according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Yunnan-Guizhou, he tried former governor Fu Gang, proved his corruption, and punished him by law.

sentences.zh: 又按問雲南巡撫江蘭諱災，得實，褫江蘭職。

translations.literal: He also investigated Yunnan Governor Jiang Lan for concealing disasters; the charge was proved and Jiang Lan was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He also investigated Yunnan governor Jiang Lan for concealing disasters, proved the charge, and stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 時倮夷不靖，疏陳江蘭所奏不實，辦理草率，帝嘉其公正。

translations.literal: At the time the Luo tribes were unsettled; he memorialized that Jiang Lan's reports were untrue and his handling perfunctory, and the Emperor praised his fairness.
translations.idiomatic: With the Luo tribes in unrest, he reported that Jiang Lan's accounts were false and his handling slipshod, and the emperor praised his impartiality.

sentences.zh: 遂親赴黃草壩督兵分路進剿，擒賊首李文明等，遣降倮入箐招諭，曉以利害，夷眾五十二寨悔罪輸誠；

translations.literal: He then went in person to Huangcaoba to direct troops advancing by separate routes, captured bandit leaders such as Li Wenming, sent surrendered Luo into the ravines to offer persuasion, explained advantage and harm, and fifty-two Yi stockades repented and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He went in person to Huangcaoba to direct a multi-pronged campaign, captured leaders such as Li Wenming, sent surrendered Luo into the ravines to preach terms, and won the submission of fifty-two Yi stockades.

sentences.zh: 以土司苛派擾夷，立牌申禁：優詔褒賚，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Because native chiefs made harsh exactions that troubled the Yi, he erected placards forbidding the practice; he received a gracious edict of reward and was made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When native chiefs' exactions were harassing the Yi, he posted public bans; the throne rewarded him with a gracious edict and made him senior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 五年，調湖廣，督師剿襄陽青、藍、黃三號教匪。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Huguang and directed the army in suppressing the Xiangyang Green, Blue, and Yellow sect rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to Huguang to command the campaign against the Green, Blue, and Yellow sect rebels at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 會長齡等已敗賊瓦房口，書麟以東川、保豐為糧運要路，親往截剿。

translations.literal: Changling and others had already defeated the bandits at Wafangkou; Shu Lin, because Dongchuan and Baofeng were key routes for grain transport, went in person to intercept and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: After Changling and others had routed the rebels at Wafangkou, Shu Lin saw Dongchuan and Baofeng as vital supply lines and went in person to cut them off.

sentences.zh: 帝念其年逾七旬，奔馳山谷間，賊情詭詐，戒毋冒險輕試。

translations.literal: The Emperor, mindful that he was over seventy and rushing through mountain valleys while the rebels were cunning, admonished him not to take risks lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful that he was past seventy, racing through mountain valleys against cunning rebels, the emperor warned him not to take reckless chances.

sentences.zh: 六年，由竹山、房縣進剿徐天德，擒斬甚眾。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, advancing from Zhushan and Fangxian against Xu Tiande, he captured and killed a great many.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he advanced from Zhushan and Fangxian against Xu Tiande and killed or captured a great many rebels.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「勦賊之法，以固民心、培民氣為要。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "The method of suppressing bandits lies chiefly in securing the people's hearts and nurturing popular morale.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "The key to suppressing rebels is to secure the people's loyalty and restore their morale.

sentences.zh: 撫輯得宜，賊即是民；

translations.literal: If pacification and relief are properly applied, bandits are the people;
translations.idiomatic: Treat people well and rebels become ordinary subjects again;

sentences.zh: 任其失所，民即是賊。

translations.literal: if they are left homeless, the people become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: leave them homeless and subjects become rebels.

sentences.zh: 」帝俞之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 川匪苟文明等由陝西平利越老林圖竄房縣，偕長齡、明亮進擊，遇賊獅子崖，大敗之；

translations.literal: Sichuan bandits Gou Wenming and others crossed from Pingli in Shaanxi over the old forest routes intending to flee into Fangxian; together with Changling and Mingliang he advanced to attack, met the bandits at Shiziya, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan rebels led by Gou Wenming slipped from Pingli in Shaanxi through the old forest paths toward Fangxian; Shu Lin joined Changling and Mingliang, met them at Lion Cliff, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 復分兵伏佘家溝、高尖山，天德等來襲，卻之。

translations.literal: He again divided his forces to ambush at Shejiagou and Gaojianshan; Tiande and others came to attack and were repulsed.
translations.idiomatic: He then set ambushes at Shejiagou and Gaojianshan and beat back an attack by Tiande and his men.

sentences.zh: 疏請於襄陽添設提督，移協鎮於鄖陽、竹山二處。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting that a provincial military commander be added at Xiangyang and that deputy commanders be moved to Yunyang and Zhushan.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to establish a provincial commander at Xiangyang and to shift deputy garrisons to Yunyang and Zhushan.

sentences.zh: 天德等屯聚茅倫山，令孫清元等分隊破之。

translations.literal: Tiande and others gathered at Maolunshan; he ordered Sun Qingyuan and others to break them in separate detachments.
translations.idiomatic: When Tiande and his followers held Maolun Mountain, he sent Sun Qingyuan and others in separate columns to defeat them.

sentences.zh: 因病乞解職，遣侍衛率御醫馳視。

translations.literal: He begged to resign on account of illness; the court sent a bodyguard leading an imperial physician to hurry to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him to request relief; the court dispatched a bodyguard with an imperial physician to attend him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒於軍，帝深惜之，贈太子太傅，封一等男爵，以子吉郎阿嗣，諡文勤。

translations.literal: Before long he died in camp; the Emperor deeply regretted it, posthumously made him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed him as first-class baron, with his son Jilang'a succeeding, posthumous name Wenqin.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in the field; the emperor mourned him deeply, posthumously made him grand tutor of the heir apparent and first-class baron, with his son Jilang'a as heir, and gave him the posthumous name Wenqin.

sentences.zh: 尋以倭什布治餉遲誤，詔斥書麟知而不舉，念其清廉公正，治軍成勞，奠醊恩禮仍有加焉。

translations.literal: Soon because Wo-shi-bu was slow in managing supplies, an edict rebuked Shu Lin for knowing and not reporting; yet mindful of his integrity and fairness and his established merit in governing the army, the rites of sacrifice and libation were still augmented.
translations.idiomatic: When Wo-shi-bu's delays in supply were exposed, an edict faulted Shu Lin for failing to report what he knew; yet remembering his integrity and his success in the field, the court still enhanced the funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 弟廣厚，乾隆四十三年進士。

translations.literal: His younger brother Guanghou passed the civil examinations in the forty-third year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Guanghou became a jinshi in Qianlong 43.

sentences.zh: 由工部主事歷御史，出為江西吉南贛寧道，遷甘肅按察使。

translations.literal: From a principal clerk in the Ministry of Works he rose through censor, went out as Jiangxi Jianan-Ganning Circuit intendant, and was transferred to Gansu surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from a clerk in the Ministry of Works to censor, then served as intendant of the Jianan-Ganning circuit in Jiangxi before becoming Gansu surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，偕總兵吉蘭泰擊教匪張映祥、楊天柱於鞏昌、秦州，進蹙諸白水江，殲焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiaqing, together with Regional Commander Jilantai he attacked sect rebels Zhang Yingxiang and Yang Tianzhu at Gongchang and Qinzhou, advanced to press them at the Baishui River, and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiaqing he joined Regional Commander Jilantai to fight sect rebels Zhang Yingxiang and Yang Tianzhu at Gongchang and Qinzhou, drove them to the Baishui River, and destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 遷江西布政使，調甘肅。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jiangxi provincial treasurer and then to Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He became Jiangxi provincial treasurer and was then transferred back to Gansu.

sentences.zh: 賊出沒於岷州、禮縣間，廣厚督兵由岷州遮羊鋪遏其衝，保完善之地，境內乂安。

translations.literal: Bandits appeared between Minzhou and Lixian; Guanghou directed troops from Minzhou to block them at Zheyangpu, protected secure areas, and the territory within the borders was at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels ranged between Minzhou and Lixian, Guanghou led troops from Minzhou to block them at Zheyangpu, secured the settled districts, and restored peace within the province.

sentences.zh: 調廣東，坐與總督那彥成遊宴，解職，予三等侍衛，為庫車辦事大臣，調哈喇沙爾。

translations.literal: Transferred to Guangdong, he was punished for feasting and touring with Governor-General Nayancheng, was dismissed, given the rank of third-class bodyguard, made Kuche frontier commissioner, and transferred to Karashahr.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Guangdong, he was dismissed for banqueting with Governor-General Nayancheng, given third-class bodyguard rank, appointed frontier commissioner at Kuche, then transferred to Karashahr.

sentences.zh: 官至安徽、湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: He rose to the posts of Governor of Anhui and Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually served as governor of Anhui and Hunan.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 覺羅吉慶，隸正白旗。

translations.literal: Aisin Gioro Jiqing belonged to the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqing of the Aisin Gioro clan belonged to the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 父萬福，騎都尉，官江寧將軍，兼散秩大臣。

translations.literal: His father Wanfu was a commandant of cavalry, served as General at Jiangning, and was concurrently an extraordinary-rank minister.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wanfu was a commandant of cavalry who served as Jiangning general and also held extraordinary ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 吉慶由官學生補內閣中書，遷侍讀，歷御史。

translations.literal: Jiqing from the Imperial School was appointed Grand Secretariat secretary, was transferred to reader, and served as censor.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqing entered service from the Imperial School as a Grand Secretariat secretary, became a reader, and served as censor.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十年，嗣世職。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year of Qianlong he inherited the hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 50 he inherited his family's hereditary post.

sentences.zh: 擢鑲白旗蒙古副都統，累遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Commander of the Mongol Bordered White Banner and successively rose to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commander of the Mongol Bordered White Banner and eventually became vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 命赴山東、湖南、湖北、河南讞獄，均稱旨，調戶部。

translations.literal: Ordered to go to Shandong, Hunan, Hubei, and Henan to try capital cases, in each case he met with imperial approval and was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to try capital cases in Shandong, Hunan, Hubei, and Henan, he pleased the throne in each province and was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，出為山東巡撫，歲祲，截留漕米三十萬石，撥豫、東軍船運米賑饑。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he went out as Governor of Shandong; the year was famine-stricken, and he detained three hundred thousand piculs of transport grain and allocated Henan and Shandong military grain boats to carry rice for famine relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year he became governor of Shandong; when famine struck, he retained three hundred thousand piculs of transport grain and used Henan and Shandong military grain boats to deliver relief.

sentences.zh: 調浙江，閩海漁船赴浙洋剽掠，吉慶於島嶴編保甲，禁米出洋，嚴緝代賣盜贓；

translations.literal: Transferred to Zhejiang, when Fujian fishing boats came to Zhejiang waters to plunder, Jiqing organized baojia on the islands, forbade rice to be taken overseas, and strictly hunted those who sold stolen goods on others' behalf.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Zhejiang he faced Fujian fishing boats raiding Zhejiang waters; he organized local militia on the islands, banned grain exports overseas, and cracked down on fencing stolen goods.

sentences.zh: 兼署提督，獲海盜陳言等，及臨海邪匪李鶴皋，置之法。

translations.literal: He also served as acting provincial military commander, captured pirates such as Chen Yan, and the heterodox bandit of Linhai Li Hegao, and punished them by law.
translations.idiomatic: Acting as provincial military commander, he captured pirates including Chen Yan and the Linhai rebel Li Hegao and executed them.

sentences.zh: 鹽政岳謙執拗病民，劾罷之，遂兼鹽政。

translations.literal: Salt Controller Yue Qian was obstinate and harmed the people; he impeached and dismissed him and then concurrently held the salt post.
translations.idiomatic: When salt controller Yue Qian's stubborn policies were harming the people, he impeached and removed him and took over the salt administration himself.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，擢兩廣總督，劾水師提督路超吉不勝任，貶超吉秩。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he was promoted to Governor-General of the Two Guangs, impeached Naval Commander Lu Chaoji as incompetent, and reduced Chaoji's rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1 he became governor-general of the Two Guangs, impeached naval commander Lu Chaoji for incompetence, and demoted him.

sentences.zh: 二年，廣西西隆亞稿寨苗匪句結貴州仲苗，竄踞八渡，率提督彭承堯進剿，克其要隘。

translations.literal: In the second year, Miao bandits of Yagao stockade in Xilong, Guangxi, colluded with Zhong Miao of Guizhou, fled to occupy Badu, and he led Provincial Commander Peng Chengyao forward to suppress them and captured their key passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Miao rebels of Yagao stockade in Guangxi's Xilong joined Guizhou Zhong Miao and seized Badu; he led Provincial Commander Peng Chengyao against them and took their strong points.

sentences.zh: 黔苗潛渡百樂窺泗城，令副將德昌等分路攻撲，毀苗砦十有九；

translations.literal: Guizhou Miao secretly crossed at Baile to spy on Sicheng; he ordered Deputy Generals Dechang and others to attack by separate routes and destroyed nineteen Miao stockades.
translations.idiomatic: When Guizhou Miao slipped across at Baile toward Sicheng, he sent Deputy General Dechang and others on separate routes and destroyed nineteen stockades.

sentences.zh: 進攻亞稿，至戛雄遇賊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Advancing against Yagao, at Gaxiong he met the bandits and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the attack on Yagao, he met the rebels at Gaxiong and routed them.

sentences.zh: 永豐、百樂等苗目渡江降，給酒食，令回寨招撫。

translations.literal: Miao chiefs of Yongfeng, Baile, and others crossed the river to surrender; he gave them food and drink and ordered them back to their stockades to win others over.
translations.idiomatic: Miao chiefs from Yongfeng, Baile, and elsewhere crossed the river to surrender; he fed them and sent them back to their stockades to win others over.

sentences.zh: 亞稿山路陡峻，選精卒由間道潛襲，克其巢，斬首千級，以功加太子太保，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: The mountain roads of Yagao were steep; he chose elite troops to strike secretly by a bypath, captured their lair, and beheaded a thousand; for his merit he was made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted the peacock feather with double eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Yagao's mountain paths were steep; he sent picked troops along a hidden route, stormed the rebel nest, and took a thousand heads; for this he was made senior guardian of the heir apparent and given the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 亞稿之捷，投誠者十餘寨，惟附近那地、小河、廣平、蒙裡等寨猶恃險抗拒，會雲南兵至，會剿，盡克之。

translations.literal: After the victory at Yagao more than ten stockades submitted; only nearby Nadu, Xiaohe, Guangping, Mengli, and other stockades still relied on terrain to resist; when Yunnan troops arrived they joined in the campaign and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yagao victory more than ten stockades submitted, but Nadu, Xiaohe, Guangping, Mengli, and neighboring stockades still held out; Yunnan troops arrived, joined the campaign, and took them all.

sentences.zh: 賊首龍登連父子乞降，粵境悉平。

translations.literal: Bandit leaders Long Denglian, father and son, begged to surrender, and the Guangdong territory was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leaders Long Denglian and his son surrendered, and Guangdong was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 六年，命協辦大學士、總督如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was ordered to serve as Associate Grand Secretary while retaining the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made associate grand secretary while remaining governor-general.

sentences.zh: 吉慶居官廉而察吏疏，博羅縣重犯越獄，司府徇隱；

translations.literal: Jiqing in office was incorrupt but lax in scrutinizing subordinates; in Boluo a serious criminal escaped prison and the prefectural offices shielded the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqing was honest in office but lax toward his subordinates; when a serious criminal escaped jail in Boluo, prefectural officials covered it up.

sentences.zh: 又通省贓罰銀按縣派徵，為臬司漏規。

translations.literal: Moreover, throughout the province fines in lieu of punishment were levied by county assignment as a leak-line profit for the provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: Fines levied province-wide by county were also being skimmed as secret fees by the provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 事並上聞，詔斥其因循。

translations.literal: Both matters were reported to the throne, and an edict rebuked his procrastination.
translations.idiomatic: When both matters reached the throne, an edict rebuked his slackness.

sentences.zh: 陳爛屐四者，於博羅山中糾眾為添弟會，知府伊秉綬請發兵往捕，吉慶為提督孫全謀所蔽，未許。

translations.literal: Chen Lanji, the Fourth, in the Boluo mountains gathered a crowd into the Tiandi Society; Prefect Yi Bingshou asked to send troops to capture them, but Jiqing, misled by Provincial Commander Sun Quanmou, did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Lanji the Fourth rallied a Tiandi Society band in the Boluo hills; Prefect Yi Bingshou asked for troops, but Jiqing, swayed by Provincial Commander Sun Quanmou, refused.

sentences.zh: 七年，陳爛屐四果剽掠作亂，擾及數縣，遣師擒斬之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Chen Lanji the Fourth did indeed plunder and rise in revolt, disturbing several counties; he sent troops who captured and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Chen Lanji the Fourth did raid and rebel, troubling several counties; Jiqing sent troops who captured and killed him.

sentences.zh: 餘黨曾鬼六复勾結永安諸賊相繼起，吉慶馳往剿捕，請調江西兵二千為助。

translations.literal: The remnant party Zeng Guiliu again colluded with Yong'an bandits who rose one after another; Jiqing hurried to suppress them and requested two thousand Jiangxi troops as aid.
translations.idiomatic: Remnant leader Zeng Guiliu then joined Yong'an rebels in a fresh uprising; Jiqing rushed to suppress them and asked for two thousand troops from Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 詔斥其張皇，始疑之。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked his alarmism, and the court began to doubt him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked his alarmism, and the court began to doubt him.

sentences.zh: 尋敗賊於義容墟，曾清浩率眾四千餘人繳械降。

translations.literal: Soon he defeated the bandits at Yirongxu; Zeng Qinghao led more than four thousand men to surrender their weapons.
translations.idiomatic: He soon routed the rebels at Yirong market, and Zeng Qinghao surrendered with more than four thousand men.

sentences.zh: 全謀擒賊渠薛文勝，暨匪眾四百餘，悉誅之。

translations.literal: Quanmou captured bandit leader Xue Wensheng together with more than four hundred rebels and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Quanmou captured rebel leader Xue Wensheng and more than four hundred followers and executed them all.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝以吉慶奏報前後不符，措置失當，罷協辦大學士，留總督任，命那彥成往按。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the Emperor, because Jiqing's memorials before and after did not agree and his measures were improper, removed him as Associate Grand Secretary but kept him as governor, and ordered Nayancheng to go investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When reports reached the throne, the emperor found Jiqing's accounts inconsistent and his handling inept, stripped him of associate grand secretary rank but kept him as governor, and sent Nayancheng to investigate.

sentences.zh: 吉慶復奏永安降匪多，請留兵防範，詔斥《頁》結局，解任聽勘。

translations.literal: Jiqing again memorialized that there were many surrendered bandits in Yong'an and asked to retain troops for defense; an edict rebuked his perfunctory conclusion, removed him from office, and ordered him to await investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqing then reported many surrendered rebels in Yong'an and asked to keep troops on guard; the throne rebuked his slipshod wrap-up, dismissed him, and ordered him to await trial.

sentences.zh: 巡撫瑚圖禮素與有隙，既奉密諭诇察，遂疏劾其疲輭不職，那彥成猶未至，獨鞫之，據高坐，設囚具，隸卒故加訶辱。

translations.literal: Governor Hutuli had long been at odds with him; having received a secret edict to investigate, he memorialized impeaching him as slack and negligent; Nayancheng had not yet arrived, yet Hutuli alone tried him, sat on a high seat, set out prisoner implements, and clerks deliberately added abuse and insult.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Hutuli, who had long been his enemy, received a secret order to investigate and impeached him for incompetence. Before Nayancheng arrived, Hutuli tried him alone from a high seat with shackles ready, while clerks deliberately heaped abuse on him.

sentences.zh: 吉慶恚曰：「某雖不肖，曾備位政府，不可受辱傷國體！

translations.literal: Jiqing said in anger: "Though I am unworthy, I once held a place in the government and cannot suffer insult that wounds the dignity of the state!
translations.idiomatic: Jiqing said in fury: "However unworthy I am, I once served in the central government and will not endure insults that dishonor the state!

sentences.zh: 」因自戕。

translations.literal: " and therefore killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: " He then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，命那彥成陳狀，尋以吉慶素廉潔，治匪有功，無故輕生，詔免追論。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he ordered Nayancheng to report the facts; soon, because Jiqing had always been incorrupt, had merit in suppressing bandits, and had taken his life without cause, an edict exempted further prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this, the emperor ordered Nayancheng to report the facts; mindful of Jiqing's integrity and success against bandits, and that he had died without due cause, the throne waived further prosecution.

sentences.zh: 子壽喜，仍襲世職，坐事黜，以弟常喜嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shouxi still inherited the hereditary office but was dismissed for an offense; his younger brother Changxi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouxi inherited the family post but was dismissed for misconduct; his younger brother Changxi succeeded instead.

sentences.zh: 覺羅長麟，字牧庵，隸正藍旗。

translations.literal: Aisin Gioro Zhanglin, courtesy name Mu'an, belonged to the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanglin of the Aisin Gioro clan, courtesy name Mu'an, belonged to the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十年進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year of Qianlong he passed the civil examinations and was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Qianlong 40 and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 貌奇偉，明敏有口辯，居曹有聲。

translations.literal: His appearance was strikingly imposing; he was sharp and eloquent, and made a name in the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and striking in appearance, sharp and articulate, he quickly won a reputation in his bureau.

sentences.zh: 歷郎中，出為福建興泉永道，累遷江蘇布政使。

translations.literal: He served as director, went out as Fujian Xingquan-Yong Circuit intendant, and was repeatedly promoted to Jiangsu provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director, served as intendant of Fujian's Xingquan-Yong circuit, and was promoted to Jiangsu provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，召授刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year he was recalled to the capital as vice minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，授山東巡撫，責所屬濬河道，修四十一州縣城工；

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he was appointed Governor of Shandong, charged his subordinates with dredging river channels, and repaired city works in forty-one prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year he became governor of Shandong, ordered his subordinates to dredge rivers, and repaired city walls in forty-one prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 捕鉅野、汶上劇盜田玉堂等，置之法：詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: He captured the major bandits Tian Yutang and others of Juye and Wenshang and punished them by law; an edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: He captured major bandits such as Tian Yutang in Juye and Wenshang and executed them; the throne commended him.

sentences.zh: 劾萊州知府徐大榕治平度州民羅有良獄，誤擬，大榕訴於京，刑部尚書胡季堂等往鞫，不直長麟。

translations.literal: He impeached Laizhou Prefect Xu Darong for mishandling the case of the Pingdu commoner Luo Youliang with an erroneous sentence recommendation; Darong appealed to the capital, Minister of Punishments Hu Jitang and others went to try the case, and Zhanglin was not upheld.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Laizhou prefect Xu Darong for a wrongful sentence in the case of Luo Youliang of Pingdu; Darong appealed to Beijing, Minister Hu Jitang investigated, and ruled against Zhanglin.

sentences.zh: 帝以防河有勞，特寬之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because of his merit in river defense, specially leniently treated him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spared him on account of his work on river control.

sentences.zh: 復以審擬濱州舉人薛對元罪失實，褫職，留修城工。

translations.literal: Again, because his review of the guilt of Binzhou licentiate Xue Duiyuan was not substantiated, he was stripped of office but retained to supervise city repairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was again stripped of office when his judgment in the case of Binzhou licentiate Xue Duiyuan proved unfounded, but was kept on to supervise city repairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Governor of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 嘗私行市井間訪察民隱，擒治強暴，禁革奢俗，清漕政，斥貪吏，為時所稱。

translations.literal: He once went privately into the markets to investigate the people's hidden grievances, captured and punished the violent, forbade extravagant customs, cleared up grain transport administration, and expelled greedy officials, and was praised by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: He sometimes toured the markets incognito to learn the people's grievances, punished bullies, banned wasteful customs, reformed grain transport, and expelled corrupt officials, winning wide praise.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，調山西。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he was transferred to Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year he was transferred to Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 入覲時，有市人董二誣告逆匪王倫潛匿山西某家，和申於宮門前言，務坐以逆黨。

translations.literal: When he entered audience, a townsman Dong Er falsely accused the rebel Wang Lun of hiding in a certain household in Shanxi; Heshen spoke of it before the palace gate and insisted on treating them as rebels.
translations.idiomatic: During an imperial audience, a townsman named Dong Er falsely claimed that rebel Wang Lun was hiding in a Shanxi household; Heshen pressed the case at the palace gate and demanded a treason conviction.

sentences.zh: 長麟至官，訪悉某實董仇家，​​故傾陷，慨然曰：「吾發垂白，奈何滅人族以媚權相？

translations.literal: When Zhanglin reached his post and investigated, he learned that the household was in fact Dong's enemy's family and had been framed; he said with indignation: "My hair is already turning white—how can I destroy a clan to please a powerful minister?
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he found the accused family was Dong Er's personal enemy and had been framed; he declared: "My hair is already white—how can I destroy a whole clan to please a powerful minister?

sentences.zh: 」終反坐董二，和珅大忤。

translations.literal: " In the end he instead convicted Dong Er, and Heshen was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " He instead convicted Dong Er, to Heshen's great displeasure.

sentences.zh: 調浙江，擢兩廣總督，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Transferred to Zhejiang, he was promoted to Governor-General of the Two Guangs and made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Zhejiang, he became governor-general of the Two Guangs and junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 整頓水師，擒獲海盜。

translations.literal: He reorganized the naval forces and captured pirates.
translations.idiomatic: He reorganized the navy and captured pirates.

sentences.zh: 六十年，調署閩浙。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he was transferred to act as Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year he was made acting governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 會將軍魁倫劾總督伍拉納、巡撫浦霖貪縱，並閩省庫藏虧絀事，命長麟按治，未得實，詔切責，乃奏婪索納賄狀。

translations.literal: When General Kuilun impeached Governor-General Wulana and Governor Pulai for greed and indulgence, together with deficits in the Fujian provincial treasury, Zhanglin was ordered to investigate; he did not obtain proof at first, was rebuked by edict, and then memorialized the facts of extortion and bribery.
translations.idiomatic: When General Kuilun impeached Governors-General Wulana and Pulai for corruption and Fujian treasury deficits, Zhanglin was sent to investigate; failing at first, he was rebuked, then reported extortion and bribery.

sentences.zh: 伍拉納故和珅姻戚，帝疑長麟瞻徇，並斥其平日沽名取巧，奪職，予副都統銜，赴葉爾羌辦事。

translations.literal: Wulana was a relative by marriage of Heshen; the Emperor suspected Zhanglin of shielding him and also rebuked his usual reputation-seeking tricks, stripped him of office, gave him vice-commander rank, and sent him to Yarkand on frontier duty.
translations.idiomatic: Wulana was related to Heshen by marriage; the emperor suspected Zhanglin of favoritism, rebuked his reputation-seeking, stripped his rank, and sent him to Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 尋授庫爾喀拉烏蘇領隊大臣，調喀什噶爾參贊大臣。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed expedition leader at Kurkara Usu and transferred to Kashgar commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made expedition leader at Kurkara Usu, then Kashgar commissioner.

sentences.zh: 奏減回子王公年班進京行李，以卹驛站。

translations.literal: He memorialized reducing the annual Beijing tribute luggage of Muslim princes and nobles to spare the courier stations.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to reduce the baggage allowances for Muslim princes traveling to Beijing, to spare the courier stations.

sentences.zh: 罷回民土貢。

translations.literal: He abolished the local tribute from Hui commoners.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished local tribute levies on Hui commoners.

sentences.zh: 有邊警，請調兵堵剿，詔以張皇斥之。

translations.literal: When there was a frontier alarm he requested troops to block and suppress; an edict rebuked him for alarmism.
translations.idiomatic: When border trouble arose he asked for troops; an edict rebuked his alarmism.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，授雲貴總督，調閩浙。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he was appointed Governor-General of Yunnan-Guizhou and transferred to Fujian-Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4 he became governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou, then Fujian-Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 五年，調陝甘。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Shaanxi-Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to Shaanxi-Gansu.

sentences.zh: 時教匪未靖，勸民築堡團練，令川、陝、豫、楚交界處，一體仿行，募精壯難民入伍。

translations.literal: At the time sect rebels were not yet pacified; he urged the people to build stockades and organize militia, ordered the border junctions of Sichuan, Shaanxi, Henan, and Hubei to follow suit uniformly, and recruited able-bodied refugees into the army.
translations.idiomatic: With sect rebels still active, he urged stockades and militia, extended the policy to the Sichuan-Shaanxi-Henan-Hubei borderlands, and enrolled able refugees.

sentences.zh: 督師敗伍金柱於唐家河，又擊於傅家鎮。

translations.literal: He directed the army to defeat Wu Jinzhu at Tangjia River and again struck at Fujia Town.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Wu Jinzhu at Tangjia River and again at Fujia Town.

sentences.zh: 將軍富成來援，戰歿。

translations.literal: General Fucheng came to reinforce and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: General Fucheng came to reinforce and was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 复偕固原提督慶成擊賊於沔陽乾溝河。

translations.literal: Again together with Guyuan Provincial Commander Qingcheng he attacked bandits at the Qiangou River in Mianyang.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined Guyuan commander Qingcheng to attack rebels at Qiangou River in Mianyang.

sentences.zh: 六年，迭敗高天德、馬學禮於鐵爐川、舊州鋪、綱廠、武關，擒襄陽賊首馬應祥，詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he repeatedly defeated Gao Tiande and Ma Xueli at Tieluchuan, Jiuzhoupu, Gangchang, and Wuguan, captured Xiangyang bandit leader Ma Yingxiang, and received an edict of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he repeatedly defeated Gao Tiande and Ma Xueli, captured Xiangyang rebel leader Ma Yingxiang, and won imperial praise.

sentences.zh: 尋以副將蕭福祿搜捕汧陽悄悄會匪，濫殺邀功，仁宗疑之，诇察得實，斥長麟徇庇，停​​其議敘。

translations.literal: Soon because Deputy General Xiao Fulu in searching for secret society bandits in Qianyang killed indiscriminately to claim merit, the Renzong Emperor suspected it, investigation proved the facts, and Zhanglin was rebuked for shielding wrongdoers and his merit commendation was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: When Deputy General Xiao Fulu massacred Qianyang secret-society suspects to claim credit, the emperor investigated, found Zhanglin had shielded him, and suspended his commendation.

sentences.zh: 又以傅家鎮之戰，漫無籌措，致富成陣亡。

translations.literal: Also because in the battle at Fujia Town he had no plan whatsoever, Fucheng died in formation.
translations.idiomatic: He was also faulted for the battle at Fujia Town, where his lack of planning led to Fucheng's death.

sentences.zh: 七年，召回京，降署吏部侍郎，遷禮部尚書，兼都統。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was recalled to the capital, demoted to acting Vice Minister of Personnel, transferred to Minister of Rites, and concurrently made a banner commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was recalled, demoted to acting vice minister of personnel, made minister of rites, and given a concurrent banner command.

sentences.zh: 復命督兩廣，以母老留京。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to govern the Two Guangs but remained in the capital because his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered again to the Two Guangs, he stayed in the capital because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 八年，授兵部尚書，調刑部，兼管戶部三庫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Minister of War, transferred to Punishments, and concurrently managed the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became minister of war, then punishments, and concurrently managed the three revenue treasuries.

sentences.zh: 十年，兼翰林院掌院學士，尋協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was concurrently Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and soon made Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he became Hanlin chancellor and soon associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 十三年，命偕尚書戴衢亨察視南河。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was ordered together with Minister Dai Yuheng to inspect the Southern River.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he and Minister Dai Yuheng were ordered to inspect the Southern River works.

sentences.zh: 長麟至清江浦，聞安徽諸生包世臣習河事，親訪之，同視海口，實不高仰，用其說罷改道之議。

translations.literal: When Zhanglin reached Qingjiangpu he heard that Anhui licentiate Bao Shichen was versed in river affairs and visited him in person; together they inspected the estuary and found it was not in fact high-lying; he used Bao's proposal to stop the plan to change the channel.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingjiangpu he sought out Anhui scholar Bao Shichen, an expert on rivers; they inspected the estuary, found Bao's analysis sound, and dropped the plan to reroute the channel.

sentences.zh: 與衢亨通籌河工，具得要領，帝嘉之。

translations.literal: Together with Yuheng he planned river works comprehensively, set forth the essentials, and the Emperor commended them.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yuheng planned the river works together to general approval.

sentences.zh: 复偕衢亨清查兩淮鹽務，責鹽政每年雜費悉報部覈銷，以息浮議。

translations.literal: Again together with Yuheng he audited Lianghuai salt administration and required the salt controller to report all annual miscellaneous expenses to the ministry for verification, to quiet loose talk.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yuheng also audited Lianghuai salt finances and required full reporting of expenses to quiet rumors.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以目眚久在告，特詔解職。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, because of eye disease he had long been on leave; a special edict released him from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year prolonged eye trouble led to a special edict releasing him from office.

sentences.zh: 逾年，卒，諡文敏。

translations.literal: After more than a year he died, posthumous name Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year with the posthumous name Wenmin.

sentences.zh: 費淳，字筠浦，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Fei Chun, courtesy name Yunpu, was a native of Qiantang, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Chun, courtesy name Yunpu, was from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十八年進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Qianlong he passed the civil examinations and was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Qianlong 28 and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 歷郎中，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: He served as director and was appointed Grand Council clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director and served as a Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 出為江蘇常州知府，父憂去。

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Changzhou, Jiangsu, and left on mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Changzhou in Jiangsu but left office when his father died.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補山西太原，擢冀寧道。

translations.literal: After mourning he was appointed to Taiyuan, Shanxi, and was promoted to Jining Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he served at Taiyuan and was promoted to Jining circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 累遷雲南布政使，有惠政。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Yunnan provincial treasurer and had benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Yunnan provincial treasurer, he earned a reputation for benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 以母老乞終養，喪除，起故官。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old he begged to retire and care for her to the end; after mourning he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He retired to care for his elderly mother; after her death he returned to office.

sentences.zh: 六十年，擢安徽巡撫，調江蘇。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he was promoted to Governor of Anhui and transferred to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year he became governor of Anhui, then Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二年，疏言：「淮、徐、揚三府屬被水窪地，責州縣勸植蘆葦，以收地利。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaqing he memorialized: "In the Huai, Xu, and Yang prefectures, flooded lowlands should be urged by prefectures and counties to plant reeds to gain the land's benefit.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 2 he proposed that flooded lowlands in the Huai, Xu, and Yang region be planted with reeds.

sentences.zh: 應納錢糧，即照蘆課改折徵輸。

translations.literal: Tax grain due should then be collected according to reed duties in converted assessment and payment.
translations.idiomatic: Tax grain due should be assessed and collected as reed duties instead.

sentences.zh: 」詔議行。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 調福建，復還江蘇。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Fujian and then returned to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Fujian, then returned to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 四年，擢兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Governor-General of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 淳歷官廉謹，為帝所重，兩淮鹽政徵瑞與淳為姻家，免其迴避。

translations.literal: Chun throughout his career was incorrupt and cautious and was valued by the Emperor; Lianghuai Salt Controller Zheng Rui was related to Chun by marriage, and he was exempted from recusal.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Chun was valued for probity; Lianghuai salt controller Zheng Rui, his in-law, was exempted from recusal rules.

sentences.zh: 時南河比歲漫溢，淳以江督事繁，自陳未諳河務，乞免兼管，允之。

translations.literal: At the time the Southern River overflowed year after year; Chun, because the Jiangsu governor's duties were heavy, stated that he was not versed in river works and begged to be excused from concurrent management, which was granted.
translations.idiomatic: With the Southern River flooding yearly, he asked to be relieved of river duties as governor-general, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 命淳與總河詳議河務工程，應行分辦事具聞，帝密詢漕督蔣兆奎等優劣，諭曰：「安民首在任賢，除弊必先去貪。

translations.literal: He was ordered together with the Director-General of Rivers to deliberate in detail on river works and report what should be undertaken in separate assignments; the Emperor secretly inquired about the merits of Grain Transport Director Jiang Zhaokui and others and instructed: "Securing the people lies first in appointing the worthy; eliminating abuses must first remove the greedy.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to plan river works with the director-general, he was also secretly asked about transport officials; the emperor said: "To secure the people, appoint the worthy; to end abuses, remove the greedy.

sentences.zh: 汝操守雖優，察吏過寬。

translations.literal: Though your integrity is superior, you are too lenient in scrutinizing officials.
translations.idiomatic: Your integrity is excellent, but you are too lenient toward officials.

sentences.zh: 去一貪吏，萬姓蒙福；

translations.literal: Remove one greedy official and the myriad people receive blessing;
translations.idiomatic: Remove one corrupt official and the people benefit;

sentences.zh: 進一賢臣，一方受惠。

translations.literal: advance one worthy minister and one region receives benefit.
translations.idiomatic: promote one worthy minister and a whole region gains.

sentences.zh: 其悉心訪聞，慎勿迎合朕意，顛倒是非。

translations.literal: Investigate diligently and report, and take care not to cater to my wishes and invert right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Investigate carefully and do not tell me only what I wish to hear.

sentences.zh: 」淳具以實聞。

translations.literal: " Chun reported everything according to fact.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Chun reported faithfully.

sentences.zh: 有匿名訐告常州知府胡觀瀾者，下淳按治，疏糾觀瀾與江陰知縣楊世綬勒派累民，得實，請嚴譴。

translations.literal: There was an anonymous accusation against Changzhou Prefect Hu Guanlan; it was referred to Chun for investigation; he memorialized impeaching Guanlan and Jiangyin Magistrate Yang Shishou for extorting and burdening the people, proved the facts, and requested severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Changzhou prefect Hu Guanlan was anonymously accused, Fei Chun proved he and Jiangyin magistrate Yang Shishou had extorted the people and asked for severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 詔斥不先劾，以平日廉潔，覆奏無徇隱，寬之。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked him for not impeaching earlier; because of his usual integrity, when he replied that there was no favoritism he was leniently treated.
translations.idiomatic: Rebuked for not acting sooner, he was spared because of his usual integrity.

sentences.zh: 尋劾鹽巡道彭翼蒙奢侈糜費，褫翼蒙職。

translations.literal: Soon he impeached Salt Patrol Commissioner Peng Yimeng for extravagant waste and stripped Yimeng of office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon impeached salt patrol commissioner Peng Yimeng for extravagance and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 复劾漕運總督富綱私受衛弁餽銀，時富綱已調雲貴總督，命吉慶嚴鞫，置諸法。

translations.literal: Again he impeached Grain Transport Director Fu Gang for privately receiving silver from transport guards; at the time Fu Gang had already been transferred to Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general; he was ordered to be strictly tried by Jiqing and punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached transport director Fu Gang for taking bribes; Fu Gang was sent to Jiqing for trial and punishment.

sentences.zh: 漕運旗丁苦累，屢議加徵調劑，偕漕督鐵保疏陳：「原徵隨漕項下有款可撥，以裨運丁；

translations.literal: Transport banner soldiers suffered bitter burdens; repeated proposals had been made to add levies for adjustment; together with Transport Director Tie Bao he memorialized: "Under the original transport levies there were items that could be allocated to aid the transport soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: Banner transport laborers were overburdened; he and transport director Tie Bao reported that existing transport funds could aid them;

sentences.zh: 又旗丁月米，令州縣改給折色，應領運費，責糧道放給，以免層層剝削。

translations.literal: moreover, the banner soldiers' monthly rice should be given by prefectures and counties in commuted silver, and transport fees due should be paid out by the grain intendant to avoid layer upon layer of exploitation.
translations.idiomatic: monthly grain rations should be paid in silver by local officials, and transport fees issued by the grain intendant to stop skimming.

sentences.zh: 」如所請行。

translations.literal: " As requested, it was implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was adopted.

sentences.zh: 五年，邵家壩河工合龍，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when the Shaojiaba river works were joined, he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when the Shaojiaba river junction was completed, he was made junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 六年，以足疾乞歸醫治，允之，命毋解職。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, on account of foot ailment he begged to return home for treatment; this was granted, and he was ordered not to resign his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he asked to go home to treat a foot ailment; leave was granted without removing him from office.

sentences.zh: 尋稱足疾已瘳，若遵旨回籍，轉涉欺矇，詔嘉其得大臣體，賜內府藥餌。

translations.literal: Soon he said his foot ailment had healed; if he followed the edict and returned to his native place it would involve deception; an edict praised him for understanding a minister's proper conduct and bestowed palace medicines.
translations.idiomatic: When he said he had recovered but could not go home without seeming to deceive the throne, the emperor praised his integrity and sent palace medicines.

sentences.zh: 七年，宿州土匪王潮名糾眾戕官，檄鎮將剿捕。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, at Suzhou bandit Wang Chaoming gathered a crowd and killed officials; he ordered regional commanders to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Suzhou bandit Wang Chaoming killed officials; Fei Chun ordered troops to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 事定，請於宿之南平集設撫民同知，裁寧國府同知，移駐其地，並調設營汛，從之。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he requested that a subprefect for pacifying the people be established at Nanpingji south of Suzhou, that the Tongning subprefect of Ningguo Prefecture be abolished and moved to that place, and that garrisons be adjusted accordingly; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he proposed a new subprefect at Nanpingji and garrison adjustments; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 八年，召授兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was summoned and appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was recalled as minister of war.

sentences.zh: 時河決河南衡家樓，橫溢張秋以南，由鹽河入海，有妨漕運，命淳往勘治，於張秋西岸加寬裹頭，東岸加高長堤，以防溜勢北掣，南口趁汶水北注之勢，引歸河身；

translations.literal: At the time the river broke at Hengjialou in Henan and overflowed south of Zhangqiu through the salt river to the sea, harming grain transport; he was ordered to go survey and repair; on the west bank of Zhangqiu the wrapping head was widened, on the east bank the long dike was heightened to guard against the current being drawn north, and at the south mouth the momentum of the Wen River flowing north was used to return the flow to the river channel;
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River broke at Hengjialou and flooded toward Zhangqiu, he was sent to repair the works, widening the west bank and heightening the east dike, and using the Wen River to restore the main channel;

sentences.zh: 北口自大溜迤北，分導餘流，以資挽運：並仿南河刷沙法，制混江龍鐵篦船以疏淤。

translations.literal: at the north mouth the main current was guided north to divide and conduct the surplus flow to aid hauling: and following the Southern River sand-flushing method, mixed-river dragon iron-rake boats were made to dredge silt.
translations.idiomatic: at the north mouth surplus flow was diverted to aid transport, and sand-flushing boats were built on the southern river model.

sentences.zh: 明年，糧運過張秋無阻，降詔褒賚。

translations.literal: The next year grain transport passed Zhangqiu without obstruction, and a descending edict praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year grain transport passed Zhangqiu unimpeded, and he was commended.

sentences.zh: 調吏部尚書、協辦大學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel and Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He became minister of personnel and associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 十一年，偕尚書長麟按問直隸籓司書吏侵冒錢糧​​獄，鞫實，論如律。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, together with Minister Zhanglin he tried the case of Zhili provincial clerks embezzling tax funds, proved the facts, and sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he and Zhanglin tried Zhili clerks who had embezzled tax funds and punished them by law.

sentences.zh: 十二年，拜體仁閣大學士，管理工部，兼管戶部三庫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Entirety, managed the Ministry of Works, and concurrently managed the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he became grand secretary of the Hall of Entirety, managed the Ministry of Works, and the three revenue treasuries.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以庫銀被竊，鐫秩留任。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, because treasury silver was stolen, his rank was cut but he retained his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year treasury silver was stolen and his rank was reduced, though he kept his post.

sentences.zh: 已，复坐失察工部書吏冒領三庫銀，詔切責，削宮銜，左遷侍郎，調兵部。

translations.literal: Soon he was again punished for failing to detect Ministry of Works clerks fraudulently drawing three-treasury silver; an edict sharply rebuked him, stripped his palace rank, demoted him to vice minister, and transferred him to War.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was rebuked again for failing to detect clerks fraud in the treasuries, stripped of palace rank, and demoted to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 逾年，复授工部尚書。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was again appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was again made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒，復大學士，諡文恪，祀雲南名宦。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died; he was posthumously restored to grand secretary, posthumous name Wenkai, and enshrined among Yunnan's famous officials.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year, was posthumously restored to grand secretary, given the name Wenkai, and enshrined among Yunnan's famous officials.

sentences.zh: 百齡，字菊溪，張氏，漢軍正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Bai Ling, courtesy name Juxi, of the Zhang clan, a Chinese Martial Bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Ling, courtesy name Juxi, of the Zhang clan, belonged to the Chinese Martial Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year of Qianlong he passed the civil examinations, was selected as a bachelor, and appointed editor.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Qianlong 37, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was made an editor.

sentences.zh: 掌院阿桂重之，曰：「公輔器也！

translations.literal: Chancellor A Gui valued him and said: "He has the makings of a chief minister!
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin chancellor A Gui prized him, saying: "He is grand-secretary material!

sentences.zh: 」督山西學政，改御史，歷奉天、順天府丞。

translations.literal: " He supervised Shanxi education, was changed to censor, and served as vice prefect of Fengtian and Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: " He supervised Shanxi education, became a censor, and served as vice prefect of Fengtian and Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 百齡負才自守，不干進，邅回閒職十餘年。

translations.literal: Bai Ling relied on his talent and kept himself aloof, did not seek advancement, and lingered in minor posts for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Talented and self-contained, he sought no promotion and lingered in minor posts for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 仁宗親政後，始加拔擢。

translations.literal: After the Renzong Emperor personally took power, he was at last promoted and selected.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the Renzong Emperor took power was he promoted.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，出為湖南按察使，調浙江，歷貴州、雲南布政使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiaqing he went out as Hunan surveillance commissioner, was transferred to Zhejiang, and served as Guizhou and Yunnan provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 5 he became Hunan surveillance commissioner, then Zhejiang intendant, then treasurer of Guizhou and Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to Governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 武緣縣有冤獄，諸生黃萬鏐等為知縣孫廷標誣擬大辟，百齡下車，劾廷標逮問，帝嘉之，賜花翎；

translations.literal: In Wuyuan County there was a wrongful case in which licentiates Huang Wanlin and others were by the magistrate Sun Tingbiao falsely sentenced to death; when Bai Ling took office he impeached Tingbiao and had him arrested and tried; the Emperor commended him and bestowed the peacock feather;
translations.idiomatic: At Wuyuan, magistrate Sun Tingbiao had falsely condemned licentiates including Huang Wanlin to death; Bai Ling impeached and arrested him, winning praise and the peacock feather;

sentences.zh: 洎定讞，特加太子少保。

translations.literal: when the sentence was fixed, he was specially made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: when the case was decided, he was specially made junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 十年，調廣東。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 南海、番禺兩縣蠹役私設班館，羈留無辜，為民害，重懲之；

translations.literal: In Nanhai and Panyu the corrupt clerks privately set up detention halls, held innocent people, and harmed the people; he punished them severely;
translations.idiomatic: In Nanhai and Panyu corrupt clerks ran private detention halls; he punished them severely;

sentences.zh: 劾罷縱容之知縣王軾、趙興武，嚴申禁令：詔予優敘。

translations.literal: he impeached and dismissed the magistrates Wang Shi and Zhao Xingwu who had indulged them, and strictly proclaimed the prohibition: an edict granted superior commendation.
translations.idiomatic: impeached indulgent magistrates Wang Shi and Zhao Xingwu, and strictly enforced the ban; the throne commended him.

sentences.zh: 尋擢湖廣總督。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Governor-General of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 兩湖多盜，下令擒捕，行以便宜，江、湖晏然。

translations.literal: In the Two Hu there were many bandits; he ordered capture and might act at discretion; the rivers and lakes were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang had many bandits; he ordered their capture with discretionary powers, and the region grew calm.

sentences.zh: 未幾，王軾訐百齡在粵用非刑斃命，逼勒供應，臨行用運夫二千餘名。

translations.literal: Before long Wang Shi accused Bai Ling of using illegal torture to cause death in Guangdong, coercing supplies, and on departure using more than two thousand transport laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Shi accused him of illegal torture and death in Guangdong, coerced supplies, and using more than two thousand transport laborers on departure.

sentences.zh: 總督那彥成疏劾，並及到湖北後，截留廣東會奏批摺。

translations.literal: Governor-General Nayancheng memorialized impeachment, and also cited after reaching Hubei his retention of a joint memorial dispatch from Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Nayancheng impeached him and cited his retention of a joint Guangdong memorial after reaching Hubei.

sentences.zh: 命吳熊光等按鞫，議褫職遣戍，帝原之，命效力實錄館。

translations.literal: He was ordered to be tried by Wu Xiongguang and others; deliberation stripped him of office and banished him, but the Emperor pardoned him and ordered service at the Veritable Records Office.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xiongguang and others recommended dismissal and exile; the emperor pardoned him and assigned him to the Veritable Records Office.

sentences.zh: 尋予六品頂戴，赴福建治糧餉，事竣，授汀漳龍道。

translations.literal: Soon he was given sixth-rank hat button, sent to Fujian to manage grain supplies; when the task was done he was appointed Tingzhang-Long Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given sixth rank, sent to Fujian for grain supplies, then made intendant of Tingzhang-Long circuit.

sentences.zh: 擢湖南按察使，調江蘇，以病歸。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hunan surveillance commissioner, transferred to Jiangsu, and returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He became Hunan surveillance commissioner, then Jiangsu, then retired ill.

sentences.zh: 病痊，授鴻臚寺卿，歷山東按察使，就擢巡撫。

translations.literal: When his illness healed he was appointed Chamberlain of the Court of Imperial Stud, served as Shandong surveillance commissioner, and was promoted in that post to governor.
translations.idiomatic: Recovered, he became chamberlain of the Court of Imperial Stud, Shandong surveillance commissioner, then governor.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to Governor-General of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he became governor-general of the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 粵洋久不靖，巨寇張保挾眾數万，勢甚張。

translations.literal: The Guangdong seas had long been unsettled; the great pirate Zhang Bao led tens of thousands and his power was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong waters had long been lawless; the pirate Zhang Bao commanded tens of thousands and grew formidable.

sentences.zh: 百齡至，撤沿海商船，改鹽運由陸，禁銷贓、接濟水米諸弊。

translations.literal: When Bai Ling arrived, he withdrew coastal merchant shipping, shifted salt transport by land, and banned the abuses of fencing stolen goods and supplying water and grain.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he pulled merchant ships off the coast, moved salt transport inland, and banned fencing and supply to pirates.

sentences.zh: 籌餉練水師，懲貪去懦，水師提督孫全謀失機，劾逮治罪。

translations.literal: He raised funds and trained the navy, punished greed and removed the timid; Naval Commander Sun Quanmou lost his opportunity and was impeached, arrested, and punished.
translations.idiomatic: He funded and trained the navy, punished corruption and cowardice, and impeached naval commander Sun Quanmou for missing his chance.

sentences.zh: 每一檄下，耳目震新。

translations.literal: With every dispatch sent down, ears and eyes were startled anew.
translations.idiomatic: Every order he issued shook officials into alertness.

sentences.zh: 巡哨週嚴，遇盜輒擊之沉海，群魁奪氣，始有投誠意。

translations.literal: Patrols were strict on all sides; whenever bandits were met they were struck and sunk at sea; the chieftains lost heart and only then showed willingness to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Patrols tightened; pirates were sunk on sight; the leaders lost nerve and began to talk of surrender.

sentences.zh: 張保妻鄭尤黠悍，遣硃爾賡額、溫承志往諭以利害，遂勸保降，要製府親臨乃聽命。

translations.literal: Zhang Bao's wife Zheng was especially cunning and fierce; he sent Zhu Ergeng'e and Wen Chengzhi to explain advantage and harm, and she then urged Bao to surrender, demanding that the governor come in person before they would obey.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bao's wife Zheng was fierce and clever; Bai Ling sent Zhu Ergeng'e and Wen Chengzhi to reason with her, and she urged surrender only if the governor came in person.

sentences.zh: 百齡曰：「粵人苦盜久矣！

translations.literal: Bai Ling said: "The people of Guangdong have long suffered from bandits!
translations.idiomatic: Bai Ling said: "Guangdong has suffered pirates long enough!

sentences.zh: 不坦懷待之，海氛何由息？

translations.literal: If we do not receive them with open sincerity, how can the maritime troubles cease?
translations.idiomatic: If we do not meet them openly and honestly, how will the seas ever be calm?

sentences.zh: 」遂單舸出虎門，從者十數人，保率艦數百，轟砲如雷，環船跪迓，立撫其眾，許奏乞貸死。

translations.literal: " He then went alone in a small boat out of Humen with only a dozen followers; Bao led several hundred warships, cannon thundering like peals, surrounded the boat and knelt to welcome him; he immediately pacified the crowd and promised to memorialize begging mercy for their lives.
translations.idiomatic: He sailed alone through Humen with a dozen men; Bao brought hundreds of warships, guns thundering, and knelt from surrounding boats; Bai Ling pacified the men and promised to seek mercy for them.

sentences.zh: 旬日解散二萬餘人，繳砲船四百餘號，復令誘烏石二至雷州斬之，釋其餘黨，粵洋肅清。

translations.literal: Within ten days more than twenty thousand were disbanded, more than four hundred gunboats were surrendered, and he again had them lure Wu Shier to Leizhou and behead him, released the rest of the party, and the Guangdong seas were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he disbanded twenty thousand men, collected four hundred gunboats, lured Wu Shier to Leizhou for execution, freed the rest, and cleared Guangdong waters.

sentences.zh: 帝愈嘉異之，复太子少保，賜雙眼花翎，予輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: The Emperor commended him all the more, restored him as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, bestowed the peacock feather with double eyes, and granted the hereditary office of Commandant of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him further, restored his rank as junior guardian of the heir apparent, gave him the double-eyed peacock feather, and granted a hereditary commandant of light chariots.

sentences.zh: 十六年，再乞病，回京，授刑部尚書，改左都御史，兼都統。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he again begged leave on account of illness, returned to the capital, was appointed Minister of Punishments, changed to Censor-in-Chief of the Left, and concurrently made a banner commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he returned ill to the capital as minister of punishments, then left censor-in-chief, with a concurrent banner command.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授兩江總督。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Governor-General of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 時河決王家營，上游綿拐山、李家樓並漫溢，論者謂河患在雲梯關海口不暢，多主改由馬港新河入海。

translations.literal: At the time the river broke at Wangjiaying; upstream at Mianguai Mountain and Lijialou it also overflowed; opinion held that the river trouble lay in the estuary at Yunti Pass not flowing freely, and many advocated diverting through the Magang new channel to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: When the river broke at Wangjiaying and flooded upstream, many argued the trouble was a blocked estuary at Yunti Pass and favored a new outlet at Magang.

sentences.zh: 百齡親勘下游，疏言：「海口無高仰形跡，亦無攔門沙堤。

translations.literal: Bai Ling personally surveyed the lower reaches and memorialized: "At the estuary there is no sign of high-lying terrain, nor any blocking sand dike.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying the lower river, he reported: "The estuary shows no high barrier or blocking sand dike.

sentences.zh: 其受病在上年挑河二段內積淤三千餘丈。

translations.literal: The trouble lies in the more than three thousand zhang of silt accumulated within the two river sections dredged the previous year.
translations.idiomatic: The problem is more than three thousand zhang of silt in last year's dredged sections.

sentences.zh: 又親至馬港口以下，見淤沙挑費更鉅，入海路窄。

translations.literal: He also went in person below Magang mouth and saw that dredging the silt would cost even more and the channel to the sea was narrow.
translations.idiomatic: Below Magang he found dredging costlier still and the sea outlet too narrow.

sentences.zh: 二者相較，仍以修濬正河為便。

translations.literal: Comparing the two, it was still more convenient to dredge and maintain the main channel.
translations.idiomatic: He concluded that repairing the main channel was still preferable.

sentences.zh: 並請加挑灶工尾以下河身，兩岸接築新堤，於七套增建減水壩，修復王營減壩，重建磨盤埽。

translations.literal: He also requested additional dredging below the stove-workers' tail section of the channel, new dikes on both banks, a new flood-release dam at Qitao, repair of the Wangying flood dam, and rebuilding of the Mopan sao.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed further dredging, new dikes, a flood dam at Qitao, repairs at Wangying, and rebuilding the Mopan sao.

sentences.zh: 」詔如議。

translations.literal: " An edict approved as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 百齡年逾六旬始生子，值帝萬壽日，聞之，賜名扎拉芬以示寵異，勉其盡心治河。

translations.literal: Bai Ling, past sixty, had just had a son; on the Emperor's birthday the news reached him, and he was granted the name Zhala Fen as a mark of favor and urged to devote himself to river control.
translations.idiomatic: Past sixty, he had a son; on the emperor's birthday the boy was named Zhala Fen and Bai Ling was urged to finish the river works.

sentences.zh: 次年春，諸工先後竣，漕運渡黃較早，迭加優賚，賜其子六品廕生。

translations.literal: The next spring the works were completed in succession, grain transport crossed the Yellow River earlier, and he received repeated rewards; his son was granted the privilege of a sixth-rank yinsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Next spring the works finished, transport crossed early, and his son received sixth-rank yinsheng privilege.

sentences.zh: 洪湖連年水漲，五壩壞其四，詔責急修。

translations.literal: Hong Lake had risen for years; of five dams four were broken; an edict rebuked him to repair urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Lake floods had broken four of five dams; an edict ordered urgent repair.

sentences.zh: 百齡以禮壩之決，由於河督陳鳳翔急開遲閉，以致棘手，奏劾之。

translations.literal: Bai Ling held that the Li Dam breach was because River Commissioner Chen Fengxiang had opened it late and closed it early, making matters difficult, and memorialized impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed the Li Dam breach on commissioner Chen Fengxiang opening late and closing early, and impeached him.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔被嚴譴，訴道廳請開禮壩時，百齡同批允；

translations.literal: Fengxiang was severely punished; he appealed that when the circuit offices requested opening the Li Dam, Bai Ling had jointly approved the batch;
translations.idiomatic: Chen appealed that Bai Ling had approved opening the Li Dam with the circuit offices;

sentences.zh: 又訐淮揚道硃爾賡額為百齡所倚，司葦蕩營有弊。

translations.literal: he also accused Huai-Yang Circuit Commissioner Zhu Ergeng'e, whom Bai Ling relied on, of abuses in the reed-marsh camp.
translations.idiomatic: he also accused Huai-Yang commissioner Zhu Ergeng'e, Bai Ling's favorite, of abuses in the reed camp.

sentences.zh: 言官吳雲、馬履泰並論其舉劾失當，命松筠、初彭齡往按。

translations.literal: Censors Wu Yun and Ma Lvtai both argued his promotions and punishments were improper; Songyun and Chu Pengling were ordered to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Wu Yun and Ma Lvtai criticized his personnel decisions; Songyun and Chu Pengling were sent to investigate.

sentences.zh: 帝意方鄉用，議上，專坐硃爾賡額罪，以塞眾謗。

translations.literal: The Emperor still meant to employ him; when the report came up, Zhu Ergeng'e alone was punished to silence public criticism.
